by: claude: tax back-fill 2015 onward, the four taxes the ten-year report reads (France)
note: France tax years 2015 to 2025 (calendar), from PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries "Other taxes" copies dated inside each year (it carries the capital gains and wealth tax sections; review date in each note) and the EY Worldwide Personal Tax Guide 2015-16 for the wealth tax bands. Two regimes cannot be expressed by one rate and one threshold: capital gains 2015 to 2017 (progressive income tax + social levies) and the wealth tax ISF 2015 to 2017 (bands); see those notes. From 2018: 30% flat tax and no wealth tax on securities (IFI is real estate only). Rows from 2026 were already on file.

rates.note: NOT ONE RATE: gains on securities are taxed at progressive income tax rates up to 45%, plus 15.5% social levies (5.1% deductible), plus the exceptional tax on high incomes of up to 4% (PwC Other taxes, last reviewed 30 Jan 2015). A rebate of 50% (held 2 to 8 years) or 65% (8 years or more) applies to the income tax part only. Stored: headline = 45% + 15.5% for a gain held under two years (the report realises gains every year), min = the social levies alone; the exceptional tax on high incomes is left out, as in the 2026 row.

rates.thr_note: Due only if net wealth on 1 January exceeds €1.3m; the bands then start at €800,000 (a discount applies between €1.3m and €1.4m).
rates.note: Wealth tax (ISF, impôt de solidarité sur la fortune) on worldwide net assets, due if net wealth exceeds EUR 1.3 million (2015 tax year), "progressive from 0.50%, after an allowance of EUR 800,000 to 1.5% for net wealth in excess of EUR 10 million" (PwC Other taxes, last reviewed 30 Jan 2015). NOT ONE RATE: 0.5% from €800,000 to €1.3m, 0.7% to €2.57m, 1% to €5m, 1.25% to €10m, 1.5% above €10m (bands: EY Worldwide Personal Tax Guide 2015-16 (content current on 1 July 2015), https://web.archive.org/web/20160327080125/http://www.ey.com:80/Publication/vwLUAssets/Worldwide_Personal_Tax_Guide_2015-16/$FILE/Worldwide%20Personal%20Tax%20Guide%202015-16.pdf). Stored: headline = the top band, threshold = €1.3m; applied to all of the value above €1.3m it overstates the tax below €10m.
